title: Photorealistic cinematic premium independent restaurant concept film, set…
prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic premium independent restaurant concept film, set during a busy evening in a globally relatable urban neighborhood.

The restaurant should feel contemporary, intimate, lived-in and desirable without becoming ultra-luxury.

Environment:

dark natural timber,
warm stone,
textured plaster,
brushed brass details,
deep banquettes,
small tables,
linen napkins,
glassware,
subtle framed art,
candlelight,
warm pendant lights,
open service pass,
soft haze,
large street-facing windows,
layered reflections from the city outside.

The room is nearly full but never overcrowded.
People lean toward one another in conversation.
Jackets hang on chair backs.
Servers move between tables with confidence.
A bartender works deeper in frame.

The open kitchen gives occasional glimpses of flame and steam.

No recognizable branding.
No text overlays.
No conventional food-commercial visual language.

ABSOLUTE CHARACTER LOCK — PRIMARY GUEST

Create one recurring guest and preserve identity perfectly throughout.

Late 20s to mid-30s.

Globally relatable urban professional.

Natural attractive appearance but not fashion-model perfect.

Medium complexion.

Dark hair.

Relaxed, understated confidence.

WARDROBE LOCK

Same exact outfit throughout:

dark casual evening jacket or lightweight coat,
muted neutral top,
relaxed dark trousers,
understated shoes,
minimal watch or jewellery,
no visible logos.

Same face.
Same hairstyle.
Same skin tone.
Same height.
Same body proportions.
Same wardrobe.
Same accessories.

No character morphing.

The guest never performs for camera.
Their emotional progression is subtle:

neutral → notices → slows → decides → enters → relaxes → belongs

GLOBAL CASTING

The restaurant population should feel naturally international and urban.

Include believable diversity across age, gender presentation, appearance and background.

Do not stage diversity as a visual statement.

They are simply real people spending an evening together.

Use:

couples,
groups of friends,
colleagues,
occasional solo guest,
returning regular,
staff of varied backgrounds.

No one should look like background fashion casting.

Natural wardrobe.
Natural behavior.
No choreographed laughter.
No exaggerated celebration.

0:00–0:04 — OUTSIDE LOOKING IN

CAMERA: LONG-LENS MEDIUM-WIDE / SLOW PARALLEL TRACK

Open outside on a cool evening street.

The restaurant is initially not presented as a hero façade.

Instead, the frame is partially obscured by real city life:

pedestrians crossing,
a passing taxi,
bicycle wheel,
street reflections,
someone carrying an umbrella or bag.

The primary guest walks along the pavement at a normal pace.

They are not visibly searching for somewhere to eat.

Through the restaurant window we catch only fragments:

warm amber light,
silhouettes moving,
a server crossing,
someone leaning forward while talking,
a raised glass briefly catching light,
a burst of laughter visible but initially muffled through glass.

The guest’s eyes shift toward the restaurant.

They continue walking.

No obvious reaction yet.

LIGHTING

Exterior:
cool blue-grey evening ambience.
Interior:
warm 2700–3200K practical glow.

This warm/cool contrast is essential.
AUDIO

Street dominates:

footsteps,
distant traffic,
low conversation,
bike bell,
subtle horn,
treet ambience.

Restaurant sound remains muffled behind glass.

No score yet.

0:04–0:07 — THE ROOM PULLS THEM IN

CAMERA: SIDE PROFILE TRACK / SUBTLE SLOWDOWN

Camera moves alongside the guest.

Reflections from the restaurant windows move across their face.

Through the glass:

a woman throws her head back in genuine laughter,
someone raises a glass toward a friend,
a waiter bends slightly to hear a guest,
candle flame moves naturally,
a chair shifts,
steam catches a warm shaft of light near the service pass.

No food is showcased.

The guest’s walking pace drops slightly.
Their eyes stay inside longer than they intended.

The emotional meaning:

“Something is happening in there.”

Introduce the faintest low cinematic tonal pulse beneath street ambience.

0:07–0:10 — THE DOOR OPENS

CAMERA: OVER-SHOULDER TOWARD ENTRANCE / VERY GENTLE PUSH

A couple exits the restaurant just ahead of the guest.

The door swings outward.

For approximately two seconds, the acoustic barrier disappears.

Restaurant sound spills naturally onto the pavement:

conversation,
laughter,
glass clinks,
soft music,
chair movement,
kitchen activity.

Warm interior light spills onto the sidewalk.

The guest instinctively turns more fully toward the entrance.

The exiting couple passes close to camera, creating a natural foreground wipe.

The guest hesitates for half a beat.
Then steps toward the still-closing door.
This is the first active decision.

No dialogue.
No dramatic nod.

0:10–0:14 — CROSSING THE THRESHOLD

CAMERA: CONTINUOUS REAR FOLLOW

Follow directly behind the guest through the doorway.

Do not cut at the threshold.

The transition should be physically immersive.

Cool street light remains on their shoulders for the first step.

As they move deeper:

cool exterior light falls away,
warm amber practical light moves across the jacket,
skin tone warms naturally,
city reflections disappear.

At the same time, sound transforms:

traffic softens behind,
restaurant voices become dimensional,
glasses and chair sounds gain presence,
soft music becomes clearer.

A host looks up and acknowledges the guest with a genuine small smile.

No exaggerated greeting.
No formal welcome pose.

The guest responds with a tiny nod and moves inside.

The threshold should feel like entering a different emotional climate.

0:14–0:18 — THE ROOM REVEALS ITSELF

CAMERA: SMOOTH STEADIC GLIDE AT HUMAN EYE LEVEL

Move with the guest through the dining room.
Do not cut to generic décor beauty shots.

Let details reveal themselves naturally through camera movement.

Pass close to:

a foreground wine or water glass catching candlelight,
someone leaning closer to tell a story,
a server smoothly navigating between chairs,
a hand placing another glass on a table,
someone removing a jacket,
a couple smiling quietly at each other,
bartender turning toward an unseen customer.
A server passes close to lens and briefly occludes the guest.

When the view clears, the guest has relaxed visibly.
Shoulders lower slightly.

Their gaze becomes less analytical.
Tiny smile.

The restaurant should feel like a human environment first, designed space second.

0:18–0:22 — THE RHYTHM OF THE NIGHT

CAMERA: CONTROLLED MATCH-ACTION SERIES

Increase energy without becoming a montage advertisement.

Create a connected series of tactile actions:

a hand closes the entrance door →
match movement to bartender turning a glass →
glass catches amber light →
reflection transitions into candle flame →
candle flame matches a brief flare from open kitchen →
flame disappears behind rising steam →
steam becomes foreground veil →
camera emerges beside a group laughing.

Use real-world movement to create transitions.

No hard digital effects.
No random cuts.

IMPORTANT FOOD RULE

Do not stop on finished dishes.

Food can exist:

on tables,
passing on trays,
inside peripheral frame,
at kitchen pass,
but never become the hero.

Prioritize:

faces,
hands,
glass,
steam,
fire,
fabric,
light,
proximity,
movement.

AUDIO

Create rhythmic practical sound:
glass clink,
soft chair scrape,
ice,
brief flame,
door movement,
laughter.

Subtle score begins blending with the room.

0:22–0:25 — HUMAN CONNECTION

CAMERA: OBSERVATIONAL MEDIUM / GENTLE ARC

The guest reaches a table where two friends are already seated.

Recognition is immediate but natural.
One friend stands halfway.

Quick genuine embrace or hand on shoulder.
Another pulls out a chair.

The guest sits.
Someone slides a glass toward them.

title: Photorealistic cinematic global apparel and footwear storefront film, premium…

Warm natural timber.
Brushed metal.
Textured stone.
Soft architectural lighting.
Carefully spaced garments.

One hero sneaker.
One hero jacket.
One or two complementary pieces.

No clutter.
No giant sale graphics.
No recognizable brands or logos.

The visual world should feel equally believable in London, New York, Toronto, Berlin, Dubai, Singapore, Sydney or Mumbai.

The store should feel aspirational but attainable.
Not luxury for luxury’s sake.
Not a fashion-show environment.
The story is about attention and curiosity.

ABSOLUTE CHARACTER LOCK — PRIMARY SHOPPER

Late 20s to early 30s.

Globally relatable urban professional.

Natural facial structure.

no visible logos.

Same hair.

Same bag.
Same shoes.

No posing.
No exaggerated fashion attitude.
No dramatic smile.

The entire performance should be built from tiny, believable physical changes:

normal walking pace,
eyes shift,
head begins turning,
pace slows,
one extra glance,
stop,
look back,
lean slightly toward glass,
eyes move deeper inside,
decision,
walk in.

footsteps,
distant traffic,
soft conversations,
bike bell,
shop door opening,

there is too much to look at, so almost nothing gets noticed.

Nothing.
Another.
Nothing.

one beautifully lit pair of sneakers positioned on a low textured-stone plinth beside the edge of a structured jacket.

The display is visually quieter than surrounding stores.
That restraint makes it noticeable.

The shopper continues walking.

Just attention.

laces,
edge construction.

Structured but tactile.

Soft shadows.

carefully spaced clothing rail,
warm timber,
stone,
small pools of light,

No floating prices.

jacket →
deeper interior →
entrance.

0:21–0:24 — THE APPROACH

As they move closer:

warm light increasingly reaches their clothing,
street sounds remain present,
door details become visible.

0:24–0:27 — CROSSING THE THRESHOLD

No dramatic automatic-door reveal unless architecture supports it.

neutral transition at doorway →
warm amber retail light settling across face and clothing.

interior room tone becomes clearer,
soft shoe movement,
hanger sound,
fabric movement,
quiet conversation.

title: Anatoli Kopadze: CAMERA: Handheld DV 16mm daily vlog footage. The video MUST begin with her…
prompt:
CAMERA: Handheld DV 16mm daily vlog footage. The video MUST begin with her propping the camera against a jar of flour on the kitchen counter, shooting her from a three-quarter angle as she cooks. She picks it up for close-ups of the food, then sets it back. The camera gets flour dust on the lens at one point — she wipes it with her sleeve and keeps going. Keep subtle handheld shake, drifting composition, autofocus hunting, rushed reframing when something sizzles, exposure breathing between the dark counter and the bright stove, and imperfect framing throughout. The camera itself is never visible.

LOOK: Warm kitchen lighting — a single overhead fixture casting yellowish light, the stove adding a bright warm glow on the food. Steam and smoke catch the light. Gentle film grain heavy in the shadows, slightly softened sharpness, subtle halation from the stove flame. Her face is warm and golden. It should feel like authentic footage from someone's everyday life rather than a polished commercial.

STYLE: A comfortable, slightly chaotic cooking vlog. She talks to the camera like a friend is in the room. Small laughs, pauses, fixing her hair, wiping her hands on the apron, tasting and reacting. She makes small mistakes and laughs at herself. She speaks in short, natural sentences with frequent pauses. Never rush dialogue. Leave quiet moments between lines.

CHARACTER: A beautiful woman in her late 20s. Long dark brown hair tied back in a low messy bun with a kitchen towel over her shoulder, warm olive skin, brown eyes, no makeup. She wears a cream-colored linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up and a dark green apron. Flour on her cheek. Natural, relaxed, a little messy.

SETTING: A small home kitchen in the evening. White tile counter, a gas stove with a well-used pan, a cutting board with onions and garlic, a jar of flour, a wooden spoon, a glass of red wine. The overhead light is the only source. A window above the sink shows darkness outside. Intimate and slightly cluttered.

SCENES:

The vlog opens with the camera propped against a flour jar. She chops an onion, eyes watering.
"I don't know why I keep doing this to myself."
She wipes her eye with the back of her wrist. Picks up the camera, holds it close to the cutting board.
"Look. The onion won."
Sets it back. Pours olive oil into the pan. It sizzles loud. She jumps.
She adds the onion. Steam rises into the light. She stirs.
"Okay that smells better."
She sips from a glass of wine. Looks at the camera.
"Don't judge."
She adds garlic. It sizzles harder. She moves the pan off the heat.
"Too hot. Always too hot."
She picks up the camera, selfie mode, flour on her cheek. She hasn't noticed.
"It's going to be fine. Probably."
She tastes from the wooden spoon, winces, then nods.
"Okay. Yeah. It's good."
Flour dust on the lens. She wipes it with her sleeve. A smile. The frame goes dark. Cut.

title: 参考@image1的人物、武器与场景，严格按照参考图呈现，不进行任何重新设计、不添加参考图以外的设定。
prompt:
参考@image1的人物、武器与场景，严格按照参考图呈现，不进行任何重新设计、不添加参考图以外的设定。

【人物】@image1＝身形瘦小的法师，灰色兜帽下是浅白色短发，灰蓝层叠长袍配破损流苏下摆，腰腿有护甲板与皮带。武器为插在冰面上的两件：带环箍的暗色法杖与华丽长剑。法杖始终握于左手，长剑始终握于右手，全片不得交换。
【对手】填满画面上方的巨大白色人形面孔，长发如流冰垂落，初始双眼闭合；它是活的，睁眼后会发出令人恐惧的大笑。

30秒专业2D手绘赛璐璐动画，16:9，4K，24fps。清晰的线稿与色块、有限色阶、手绘特效作画、冲击帧、速度线、拖影与破碎的形状变化；不使用任何三维渲染质感。接近日本高水准剧场版的作画水平。
【色彩】全片近乎单色的白与淡蓝高调画面，浓雾与飘落的白色花瓣及冰屑；唯一的彩色来自她的魔法——青白与金色高光。冷调背景与暖金魔法形成唯一的色彩对比。
【场景】如镜面般平整的冰封平原，倒映天空与人物；空气中持续飘落白色碎片。
【运镜】每2秒变换一次机位与取景尺度；大胆使用2D动画特有的透视夸张、镜头拉伸变形、多层视差、俯冲、旋转与快速拉远。

0-2秒｜极远景固定机位、超广角构图：她在画面下方渺小如一点，巨大的白色面孔占满上方，白色碎片缓慢飘落，冰面映出上下对称的倒影；全场只有风声。
2-4秒｜双手部特写、贴身横移：她左手握住法杖并将其自冰中拔起，右手随即握住长剑柄向上抽出，剑身划出一道细长的星形闪光，冰面裂出一圈细纹。
4-6秒｜自她背后仰拍巨脸、透视夸张：巨大面孔的双眼骤然睁开，随后嘴角上扬露出笑容并开始大笑；笑声的震动使整片冰面呈放射状爆裂，飘落的碎片被声波向上掀起。
6-8秒｜正上方垂直俯拍、快速拉远：她将法杖顿地，一道直径数百米的金色魔法阵在冰面上逐笔刻画成形并高速旋转，她立于阵心。
8-10秒｜低角度仰拍环绕、镜头拉伸：她举起长剑，地面的魔法阵分层升起化作数道垂直悬浮的光环，兜帽被气流掀开，破损流苏剧烈翻飞。
10-12秒｜跟随剑锋的高速横向甩镜：她挥剑，一道巨大的青白色新月形斩击自剑锋飞出，横贯天空直取巨脸，沿途云层与飘落碎片被一分为二。
12-14秒｜巨脸面部特写、冲击帧：斩击命中，它的脸颊被劈开一道深痕并炸出成片白色碎屑；它毫不在意，笑声反而更大，眼睛缓缓转向她。
14-16秒｜自她肩后越过接急速下摇、多层视差：巨脸自云中伸出一只巨大的手掌向下拍落；她瞬移侧闪，掌击将整片冰面砸得粉碎，下方的水柱冲天喷起。
16-18秒｜Sakuga冲击帧蒙太奇：单色线稿帧、蓝白双色剪影帧、拖影残像帧交替快切，展现她在坠落的冰块与水柱间连续闪避突进。
18-20秒｜自下向上仰望天空、快速拉远：她单手将法杖高举并旋转，天空中凭空生成数百根青白色光矛，同时朝巨脸倾泻而下如暴雨。
20-22秒｜巨脸手臂特写、破碎作画：那只巨手被光矛贯穿并整条崩解成漫天白色薄片；它依然在笑，整张脸终于完全转正面对她。
22-24秒｜正面中景急速推近、画面逐渐过曝：她将长剑插入脚下魔法阵中心，左手法杖举至最高；魔法阵反向旋转并把全场的光线全部吸入，画面亮度骤降后瞬间转为纯白。
24-26秒｜自侧面极远景、垂直构图：一道贯穿天地的巨大光刃自剑身穿过法杖的环箍射出，垂直劈开整片天空，冰面被光柱压出环形波纹。
26-28秒｜巨脸正面特写、静止冲击帧：光刃自额心将它的头颅一分为二，笑声在中途骤然中断；裂口沿着面孔向下蔓延，它的表情第一次凝固。
28-30秒｜自极低角度仰拍缓慢拉远至定格：巨大的白色面孔整体崩解成一场覆盖天空的白色暴雪落向镜面冰原；她收剑垂下双手，肩膀因喘息起伏，兜帽落回头上；画面定格在她与漫天飘落碎片的构图上。

【台词】日语，少女声，音量克制：
3秒｜"……起きたか。"
29秒｜"これで、静かになる。"

【约束】法杖全程在左手、长剑全程在右手，绝不交换；特效持续累积、只增不减；巨脸的笑声只在第26秒中断；人物服饰、武器与场景全程与参考图完全一致；动作有重量、惯性与预备动作，杜绝任何僵硬或不自然的关节角度；画面无字幕、无文字、无水印。
【音频】风雪呼啸、冰面爆裂、巨脸低沉而扭曲的大笑、光矛穿透空气的尖锐呼啸、光刃发射时的低频轰鸣；管弦乐自第6秒起加入合唱人声，第24秒被压成短暂真空后爆发，第28秒收束为只剩风声与飘落碎片的细响。

title: Create an ultra-realistic cinematic delivery-rider story with a strong orange…

title: Photorealistic cinematic premium neighbourhood salon client-proof film…
prompt:
Photorealistic cinematic premium neighbourhood salon client-proof film, contemporary, warm, human and globally relatable.

The salon should feel aspirational but believable rather than ultra-luxury: warm timber, brushed metal, large mirrors, soft daylight, warm practical lights, subtle plants, comfortable styling chairs, organized shelves, hair products placed naturally, clean workstations, textured plaster or concrete walls, realistic floor reflections, subdued ambient activity.

The environment should feel equally believable in London, Toronto, New York, Dubai, Singapore, Sydney or Mumbai without relying on any iconic local identity.

No recognizable salon branding.
No logos.
No beauty-commercial gloss.
No artificial influencer energy.

The story must feel like a real client experience reconstructed cinematically from her own words.

ABSOLUTE CHARACTER LOCK — CLIENT 01

Create one recurring female client and preserve her identity perfectly throughout the entire film.

South Asian woman, early 30s, warm medium complexion, expressive dark-brown eyes, natural facial structure, shoulder-length dark brown / near-black hair at the start, healthy but slightly shapeless style, understated everyday makeup, natural skin texture, calm professional presence.

She should look like a believable real client rather than a model.

WARDROBE LOCK

Keep the exact same clothing throughout the appointment:

soft cream or muted warm-beige knit top;
relaxed dark trousers or jeans;
minimal earrings;
one understated ring;
no dramatic jewellery;
no visible logos.

Her hairstyle may evolve only through visible salon actions.

Do not suddenly change:
face,
skin tone,
hair color,
hair length,
wardrobe,
makeup,
body proportions.

Her emotional progression should be subtle:

uncertain → heard → relaxed → curious → surprised → delighted → confident.

Never exaggerated.

ABSOLUTE CHARACTER LOCK — STYLIST

Create one recurring female stylist, late 20s to mid-30s.

Warm, attentive, observant, skilled.
Dark hair loosely tied back.
Muted black or charcoal contemporary salon workwear.
Minimal jewellery.

Same exact face, hairstyle, clothing and body proportions throughout.

She should never behave like a makeover-show host.

Her authority comes from listening and working carefully.

0:00–0:04 — “I DON’T KNOW WHAT I WANT”

CAMERA: MIRROR MEDIUM CLOSE-UP / VERY SLOW PUSH-IN

Open already inside the salon.
Client sits in the styling chair facing the mirror.
Frame her both directly and through the reflection where possible.
She gently touches the ends of her hair.
Looks at one side.
Then the other.
Tiny uncertainty.
Not insecurity.
Not sadness.

Just:

“I know something needs changing, but I don’t know what.”

Stylist approaches calmly in the mirror background.

Client looks toward her reflection and says naturally:

“I honestly didn’t know what I wanted.”

Let the sentence sound conversational, almost apologetic.

The stylist gives a small understanding smile, not a big reassuring performance.

LIGHTING

Soft natural window light across one side of client’s face.
Warm practical glow deeper in salon.
Mirror reflections must remain physically correct.

AUDIO

Real salon ambience:
soft distant hairdryer,
quiet conversation,
scissors somewhere off-camera,
brush against hair,
small ceramic cup placed down.
No music yet.

0:04–0:08 — LISTENING BEFORE CUTTING

CAMERA: OVER-SHOULDER MIRROR COMPOSITION / SLOW LATERAL SLIDE

Stylist moves beside the client rather than standing directly behind her.

This is important.

They should visually feel like two people solving something together.
Stylist gently lifts one section of hair.
Lets it fall.
Looks at length around the face.
Asks one quiet question.
Client explains using small hand movements near her cheeks and shoulders.

Perhaps she indicates:

“I want it lighter here,”

or,

“I still need to be able to tie it back.”

Dialogue can remain partially unheard except for fragments.

The stylist listens fully.
No interrupting.
No immediately reaching for scissors.
She nods once.
Touches another section.
Moves around the chair slightly.
Client watches her in the mirror.
The client’s shoulders relax a little.

The visual idea must read clearly:

before the stylist changed her hair, she understood her.

0:08–0:11 — THE DECISION

CAMERA: MEDIUM TWO-SHOT THROUGH MIRROR

Stylist gently gathers the hair to approximate the new shape.
She folds one section inward with her hand.
Lets another layer fall.
The client sees an early hint of what the final result might feel like.
Tiny expression of curiosity.

Stylist says naturally:

“I’d keep the length, but give it movement around your face.”

No technical hair jargon.
No sales language.
Client looks at herself.
Then at stylist in mirror.

Small nod:

“Okay.”

That “okay” is the trust moment.

0:11–0:16 — THE EXPERIENCE BUILDS

CAMERA: CONTROLLED MATCH-ACTION SERVICE SEQUENCE

Begin the transformation.
Do not make this a generic fast salon montage.
Every action must flow from the previous one.

BEAT 1

Close detail.
Comb sections hair cleanly.
First scissors approach.
Client watches briefly through mirror.
One clean snip.

SFX: crisp scissors.

Match the downward movement of the cut hair into water.

BEAT 2

Hair washing.
Warm water moves realistically through dark strands.
Stylist massages shampoo naturally.
No shampoo-commercial foam explosion.
Client closes eyes briefly, relaxing.

SFX: water, sink ambience.

BEAT 3

Towel wraps hair.
Match towel movement into blow-dryer motion.

BEAT 4

Stylist uses round brush and dryer.
Hair begins gaining volume and movement.
Loose strands react naturally to airflow.

BEAT 5

Final small shaping snips around face.
Stylist uses fingers to separate the layers.
Transformation must remain progressive and believable.

No hairstyle morphing between frames.
No changing hair density.
No sudden color shift.

0:16–0:20 — THE REVEAL

CAMERA: MIRROR-FIRST COMPOSITION / SLOW DOLLY FORWARD

The stylist lowers the dryer.
The room becomes slightly quieter.
She gently moves one final section of hair into place.
Client initially looks down.
Stylist steps slightly away.
Client looks up.

Hold.

Do not make her smile immediately.
She studies the reflection.
Eyes move from one side to the other.
Turns her head slightly left.
Hair falls naturally.
Turns slightly right.
Soft movement around cheek and shoulder.
She touches one side.
A genuine smile begins slowly.

Then:

“Oh… I love this.”

The line should sound spontaneous, almost surprising herself.

Stylist smiles quietly behind her.

No cheering.
No clapping.
No dramatic reveal spin.
This reaction is the emotional center of the film.

0:20–0:23 — THE SECOND LOOK

CAMERA: SIDE TRACKING / MEDIUM

Client stands and begins walking toward reception.
She naturally adjusts her bag or sleeve.
Her finished hairstyle moves with realistic weight and bounce.
Not slow-motion shampoo-ad movement.
As she passes another mirror deeper in the salon, she catches herself in it.
She keeps walking for half a step.
Then glances back briefly.
Tiny smile.
This is important.
It is involuntary.

The audience should understand:

she likes how she feels, not just how she looked during the reveal.

0:23–0:26 — THE REAL REVIEW

CAMERA: INFORMAL MEDIUM CLOSE / NATURAL HANDHELD

Near the entrance, she is no longer sitting in a formal testimonial setup.

Someone slightly off-camera asks casually:

“Happy?”

Client gives a small laugh.

Looks toward the person, not directly at lens initially.

Says:

“She actually listened to what I wanted.”

Tiny pause.

Then:

“I’d definitely come back.”

She briefly meets camera near the end, naturally.
Do not make this polished testimonial delivery.
Keep small imperfections in timing.
Real breathing.
Natural laugh.
Real ambient salon sound beneath.
This is the review.
Not written text.
Not stars.
A human reaction.

0:26–0:28 — THE STORY LEAVES THE ROOM

CAMERA: CONTINUOUS FOLLOW THROUGH DOOR

Client exits the salon into early evening.
Warm salon light stays behind her.
Cooler street light touches her face and hair.
She pulls out her phone while walking slowly.
Camera follows from slight three-quarter angle.
She begins typing or sending something naturally.
Do not show readable review copy.
Do not show social-media logos.
Do not show star ratings.

The important behavior is:

she voluntarily wants to tell someone.
Her thumb taps the screen.
Use the physical tap as a transition.

0:28–0:30 — THE NEXT APPOINTMENT

TRANSITION: MATCH CUT ON PHONE TAP

Her thumb taps screen.
Match to a different hand placing a phone down inside the same salon.

Reveal Client 02, a clearly different woman.
Different facial structure.
Different hairstyle.
Different clothing.

She sits in the same consultation chair from the opening.

The same stylist approaches.

Client 02 looks at her reflection and says casually:

“My friend recommended you.”

The stylist smiles.
Cut immediately after the sentence.
No extra explanation.
The story closes itself.

STORY LOGIC

The viewer must understand the entire journey without website text:

CLIENT DOESN’T KNOW WHAT SHE WANTS
→ STYLIST LISTENS
→ CLIENT TRUSTS HER
→ SERVICE HAPPENS
→ RESULT FEELS RIGHT
→ CLIENT SAYS WHY
→ SHE SHARES THE EXPERIENCE
→ ANOTHER CLIENT ARRIVES

The real conversion mechanism is not simply:

before → after.

It is:

being heard → feeling understood → telling someone else.

HAIR CONTINUITY / PHYSICS

Hair behavior must be extremely realistic.

Maintain exact:

hair color,
density,
strand thickness,
length continuity,
parting logic.
author: dev khanna

title: Create a 15-second cinematic mixed-media cooking sequence. One chef prepares…
prompt:
Create a 15-second cinematic mixed-media cooking sequence. One chef prepares one plate of spaghetti from beginning to end inside the same small home kitchen.

Keep the same chef, same kitchen layout, same cookware, same ingredients, and continuous cooking progress throughout the entire video. The only major change is the visual rendering style. The video moves sequentially through exactly five visual styles.

Never show multiple styles at the same time.

0–3s — PHOTOREAL LIVE ACTION A realistic chef drops dry spaghetti into a pot of boiling water. Steam rises naturally. The chef stirs once with tongs. Warm practical kitchen lighting, realistic textures and motion.

3–6s — STOP-MOTION CLAY Without changing camera position, composition, chef identity, or object placement, the entire scene smoothly becomes handmade clay stop-motion. The spaghetti is now partially cooked. The chef pours tomato sauce into a pan and stirs it. Visible clay fingerprints, tactile miniature textures, subtle stop-motion movement.

6–9s — BRIGHT 2D CEL ANIMATION The same scene transforms into clean colorful hand-drawn cel animation. The chef lifts the cooked noodles from the pot and drops them into the tomato sauce. Sauce splashes slightly as the noodles land. Bold outlines, simple graphic shadows, fluid expressive animation.

9–12s — PS1 LOW-POLY 3D The whole kitchen becomes late-1990s low-poly game graphics while preserving the exact scene layout. The chef tosses the spaghetti inside the pan. Chunky polygons, pixelated textures, simple vertex lighting, slightly stiff retro-game movement.

The environment is an enormous advanced mechanical installation with a broad open combat floor, industrial machinery, elevated service structures, deep architectural scale, dramatic practical lighting, and a huge glowing reactor.

Exactly two visually distinct giant humanoid battle mechs appear throughout the sequence. Each carries its own distinctive energy sword.

One mech fights with graceful precision, flowing redirection, controlled acrobatics and economical movement.

The opposing mech fights with sharper aggression, explosive forward pressure, powerful counters and predatory movement.

GENERATION GOAL

Create an intense cinematic sword duel between two enormous advanced combat machines whose articulation and control allow them to move like exceptionally skilled martial artists rather than stiff armored soldiers.

Their fighting is fluid, athletic and continuous, naturally incorporating rapid sword exchanges, parries, redirections, pivots, spins, evasive rotations, leaps, aerial flips, sliding recoveries and explosive changes of direction.

Despite their extraordinary agility, both machines retain convincing mechanical mass, momentum and physical weight.

0.0–5.0s — CONFRONTATION

Camera glides through the immense operations chamber toward the open central combat floor.

One mech enters with its energy sword active.

Across the chamber, the opposing mech waits near the glowing reactor and activates its own sword.

A brief moment of tension.

The two machines settle into contrasting combat stances: one calm and poised, the other aggressive and predatory.

End state: both fighters face one another across the chamber, ready to attack.

5.0–25.0s — CONTINUOUS BATTLE

Both mechs suddenly explode forward and collide in a powerful sword clash.

From this moment onward, the fight becomes one uninterrupted, flowing martial-arts-inspired duel with no resets or disconnected posing.

The battle travels naturally through the base rather than remaining in one location. The fighters move across the main floor, around machinery and service structures, through changes in elevation, and progressively toward the reactor.

Every movement flows naturally into the next. Blocks become counters. Evasions become repositioning. Spins continue into attacks. Landings immediately continue into movement.

The graceful fighter uses fluid pivots, rotations, agile evasions, controlled flips and precise sword redirection.

The aggressive fighter relentlessly pressures forward with rapid combinations, explosive lunges, powerful attacks and fast counters.

Let the choreography develop naturally as highly skilled mechanical martial arts rather than prescribing a fixed sequence of individual moves.

Allow rapid close-range exchanges, spinning attacks, jumping encounters, aerial rotations and occasional midair blade clashes when they arise naturally from momentum.

Both machines remain extremely agile while retaining believable mechanical physics. Acceleration feels powerful. Footfalls have weight. Landings hit hard. Momentum carries naturally through turns, collisions and recoveries.

Sparks burst from sword impacts. Metal surfaces react to hard contact. Nearby machinery and small debris respond naturally to the force of the battle. Energy light reflects across the surrounding architecture.

The camera stays engaged with the duel while maintaining clear screen geography and keeping both fighters readable.

End state: near the reactor, the two mechs deliver powerful opposing attacks and their energy swords collide and lock under tremendous force, producing an intense burst of sparks and energy.

25.0–30.0s — SEPARATION / UNRESOLVED ENDING

Continue directly from the locked swords.

The energy collision violently throws both fighters apart.

They slide backward across opposite sides of the chamber with heavy mechanical momentum, recover smoothly and immediately return to fighting stances.

Neither fighter is defeated.

They face one another across the enormous chamber, weapons active, ready to charge again.

Camera pulls backward and upward, gradually revealing the immense scale of the operations base, surrounding machinery, elevated structures and glowing reactor.

Cut before the next attack.

CINEMATOGRAPHY

Premium large-format cinematic photography with strong depth, scale and foreground/background parallax.

Favor approximately 28–35mm cinematic lenses during the active fight for speed, environmental depth and full-body readability, with occasional approximately 50mm coverage for brief dramatic hero moments.

Use dynamic low-angle tracking, sweeping lateral pursuit, controlled orbiting movement during close combat, aggressive but brief push-ins at major blade impacts, and wider moving compositions during leaps and aerial exchanges.

The opening begins wider and moves toward the fighters.

During the duel, camera movement evolves fluidly with the choreography rather than constantly cutting between unrelated viewpoints.

The final five seconds transition into a dramatic rising pullback and enormous wide view.

Camera movement is smooth, intentional and physically motivated, never random or excessively shaky.

Use natural cinematic motion blur, realistic lens behavior, restrained depth of field, controlled highlights from the energy weapons, atmospheric depth, realistic reflections and subtle volumetric light without obscuring the fighters.

Avoid extreme fisheye distortion, chaotic handheld movement, excessive cutting, or shallow focus that makes fast combat difficult to read.

CONTINUITY

Keep both mechs visually distinct and consistent throughout the fight.

Do not merge or duplicate them.

Maintain coherent spatial geography and continuous physical progression throughout the sequence.

MOVEMENT PRIORITY

Fluid, athletic, acrobatic mechanical martial arts with continuous momentum.

Never stiff, lumbering, marching, soldier-like, or pose-to-pose fighting.

The combat should feel fast, skilled and improvisational while still carrying the weight and power of enormous machines.

AUDIO

Heavy mechanical footsteps, servo acceleration, mechanical articulation, energy sword hums, sharp blade collisions, metallic impacts, sparks, machinery and deep reactor ambience.

Cinematic action music may build with the confrontation, drive the continuous duel, and rise into the final unresolved faceoff.

title: Create a cinematic mythological sequence inspired by the voyage of Odysseus and…
prompt:
Create a cinematic mythological sequence inspired by the voyage of Odysseus and the Sirens. Begin with an overwhelming view of the open sea, then progressively move closer until the audience discovers Odysseus aboard his ship, bound to the mast while being irresistibly drawn toward the Sirens. The visual scale should evolve from vast and majestic to intimate, dangerous, and hypnotic.

Extreme aerial wide shot over an immense dark-blue Mediterranean sea at golden dusk. A tiny ancient Greek sailing ship is barely visible between enormous rolling waves and distant rocky islands.

The camera begins extremely high and far away, then performs a long, accelerating push-in toward the ship, descending from the sky and skimming progressively closer to the ocean surface. Sea spray rushes beneath the camera as the vessel grows from a tiny silhouette into a clearly visible ship.

End state: the camera approaches the ship from behind and slightly above, revealing the deck and crew.

Continue the same forward movement onto the deck. Greek sailors row with tense, synchronized movements. Their ears are sealed with wax. Wind pulls violently at the sail and their clothing.

At the center of the ship, Odysseus is tightly bound upright to the wooden mast with thick ropes. He struggles against the restraints, chest heaving, eyes fixed toward something beyond the starboard side.

The camera sweeps past rowing sailors and pushes toward Odysseus, ending in a close view of his face.

A haunting female song emerges over the wind.

Odysseus' expression changes visibly: his eyes widen and remain locked toward the sound, his breathing becomes shallow, his jaw trembles, and he pulls desperately against the ropes. He tries to move toward the voice but cannot escape the mast.

The camera passes beside his face, follows his gaze, and rapidly pushes across the water toward a jagged rocky island ahead.

Reveal the Sirens among black coastal rocks surrounded by mist and crashing waves. They appear beautiful and supernatural rather than monstrous: pale humanlike figures with flowing hair and subtle birdlike or otherworldly features, singing toward the passing ship.

The camera glides between wet rocks, circles briefly around one Siren singing toward the sea, then turns back toward the approaching ship.

Their song becomes clearer and more hypnotic while waves crash violently below.

Cut back close to Odysseus as he strains harder against the ropes, silently demanding to be released. The sailors cannot hear him and continue rowing forward without looking toward the Sirens.

The ship narrowly passes the dangerous rocks. The Sirens remain behind while their song gradually weakens with distance.

The camera rapidly pulls upward and backward from Odysseus, past the mast and sails, returning to a monumental aerial wide shot. The ship becomes small again as it escapes into the vast open sea, leaving the Sirens' island behind.

Keep Odysseus as the same character throughout, wearing the same weathered ancient Greek clothing and remaining bound to the same central mast from his first appearance until the ship escapes.
Keep the same ship, crew, sail configuration, sea direction, and island geography throughout.
The ship always travels forward toward and then past the Sirens' island. Do not reverse its direction or duplicate characters.

Use epic live-action historical fantasy cinematography, realistic Mediterranean water, weathered wood, linen and bronze materials, natural skin texture, strong wind, sea mist, dramatic golden dusk light, and restrained supernatural beauty.

Audio: ocean wind, wooden hull creaking, rhythmic oars, crashing waves, strained breathing, rope tension, and the distant ethereal voices of the Sirens gradually becoming louder and then fading away.
No subtitles, no spoken dialogue, no modern objects.

the cake makes a tiny movement.

Barely noticeable.

He freezes.

Looks at the cake.

The cake leans slightly farther.

Music stops on a comedic note.

Ari's eyes widen.

Ari corrects RIGHT.

The cake wobbles.

Several berries tumble.

Ari catches the cake before it falls completely.

Silence.

tilted,
messy,
partially collapsed.

His shoulders drop.

Audio sounds like a degraded optical soundtrack: muffled mono, constant hiss and crackle, voices slightly distorted, wind buffeting the microphone.

[Stage 1]
0-8 seconds.
Initial state: handheld shot from a ridge overlooking dry desert hills at midday. Thin black smoke rises from scattered metallic debris in a shallow gouge in the earth below. The frame trembles as the cameraman walks forward.
Primary event: the cameraman narrates over the shot, voice muffled through the old microphone: {Something has come down in the hills outside Roswell... the Army's already here.} Two soldiers in 1947 US Army uniforms with M1 helmets enter frame from the right, one raising a gloved hand directly at the lens. He shouts: {Turn that camera off! This area is restricted — leave the premises, now!} The image jerks away as the cameraman backs off, ground and sky swinging through frame, then a hard splice cut with two white frames of leader.
End state: cut ends mid-motion; smoke column and debris field were last seen behind the two soldiers blocking the path.

[Stage 2]
8-15 seconds.
Continue from the previous stage: same desert location, same harsh midday light, same film stock and grain. This footage now reads as the Army's own documentation camera, steadier, on or near a tripod.
Primary event: soldiers move methodically through the debris field. One kneels and turns over a thin, curved metallic fragment that catches the sun with an unnatural mirror sheen; another photographs it with a period Speed Graphic press camera, its flashbulb popping <a sharp flashbulb pop and faint glass tink>. In the background, men carry a covered stretcher toward a canvas military tent. Low wind and indistinct clipped voices under the hiss.
End state: the covered stretcher disappears through the tent flap; the kneeling soldier still holds the metallic fragment. Hard jump cut with a frame of film scratch damage.

[Stage 3]
15-27 seconds.
Continue from the previous stage: interior of the same canvas tent, lit by one harsh bare bulb and a hot on-camera light, deep shadows, smoke haze in the beam. Same soldiers' uniforms carry over.
Primary event: a small grey-skinned humanoid alien, thin-limbed with an oversized hairless head and large dark eyes, lies strapped to a metal-framed field gurney with leather restraints across its chest, wrists, and legs. It arches and thrashes violently against the straps, head whipping side to side, its long fingers clawing at the restraints, emitting a piercing, unearthly shriek <a high, warbling, distorted scream that clips and crackles on the degraded soundtrack>. Three soldiers press down on its shoulders and legs by force, struggling to hold it as the gurney rattles. A fourth man in a medical coat leans in with a metal instrument. From somewhere off-frame, male laughter is heard, casual and unsettling <two or three men laughing lowly in the background>, followed by an offhand muffled voice: {Feisty little fella, ain't he.} The handheld camera pushes in slightly, jittering, occasionally losing focus on the creature's face.
End state: the alien is still restrained and writhing, soldiers still pinning it down, the creature's dark eyes turned directly toward the lens.

[Stage 4]
27-30 seconds.
Primary event: mid-struggle, the film abruptly degrades — frames slip, the image tears and flares white as if the reel runs out, ending on flickering blank leader with dust and scratches <the audio cuts to pure projector clatter and hiss>.
End state: white flickering film leader, no image, faint projector rattle.

[Maintain Consistency]
Keep the black-and-white 1947 16mm film look, grain, scratches, flicker, and degraded mono audio identical across all stages. Keep soldier uniforms (1947 US Army khaki, M1 helmets), the desert location and lighting in Stages 1-2, the tent interior in Stage 3, and the alien's identity (small grey humanoid, oversized head, large dark eyes, thin limbs, restrained on the same gurney) fully consistent. title: 🌊 Concept: The Last Lighthouse Keeper
prompt:
🌊 Concept: The Last Lighthouse Keeper

Create a 30-second ultra-realistic cinematic video titled “THE LAST LIGHT”, set on an enormous isolated lighthouse during a violent midnight ocean storm.

The entire video must be ONE SINGLE UNINTERRUPTED CONTINUOUS SHOT lasting exactly 30 seconds. No cuts, no scene transitions, no teleportation, no time skips, no duplicated characters, no sudden environment changes. Every movement must connect naturally from the previous moment.

0–5 seconds — Establishing approach

Begin with an extremely low cinematic camera flying just above a violently turbulent black ocean at night. Huge waves rise several meters high, illuminated intermittently by distant lightning. Torrential rain falls diagonally across the frame. The camera races toward a gigantic ancient lighthouse standing alone on a jagged rock formation.

The lighthouse beam slowly sweeps through the storm, briefly illuminating rain, sea spray, birds, and enormous waves. Thunder flashes reveal the scale of the environment.

The camera approaches the lighthouse at high speed and naturally rises along its outer stone wall, following the structure upward.

5–10 seconds — Entering the lighthouse

As the camera reaches a shattered window near the top, it smoothly flies through the opening without cutting.

Inside is a massive circular lighthouse chamber containing an enormous rotating Fresnel lens. The mechanical gears are turning slowly, covered with condensation and tiny droplets of rain.

An elderly lighthouse keeper wearing a heavy weathered coat rushes into frame carrying an old oil lantern. His clothes and hair are soaked from the storm.

He looks toward the enormous rotating light mechanism and realizes something is wrong.

The main lighthouse beam suddenly flickers.

10–16 seconds — The failure

The camera continuously circles around the keeper as he climbs a narrow spiral staircase toward the light mechanism.

Outside the windows, lightning repeatedly illuminates the ocean.

The lighthouse beam becomes weaker.

The keeper reaches the mechanical control system and desperately begins turning a large emergency brass wheel.

The machinery resists.

Metal gears grind realistically.

Water leaks through cracks in the stone walls.

The entire tower subtly shakes as a gigantic wave crashes against the rock below.

16–23 seconds — The impossible moment

The keeper finally forces the mechanism back into motion.

The giant Fresnel lens suddenly ignites with an intense warm golden beam.

The camera moves extremely close to the rotating lens, passing around it as the beam sweeps across the storm.

Every time the beam crosses the ocean, enormous waves become visible for a split second.

A distant cargo ship appears dangerously close to the rocks.

The lighthouse beam reaches it.

The ship immediately changes direction.

The keeper watches silently through the rain-covered window.

23–30 seconds — Cinematic climax

The camera smoothly exits through the same window and pulls rapidly backward into the storm.

The lighthouse now stands brilliantly illuminated against the enormous black ocean.

The beam rotates continuously across the sea, cutting through rain and fog.

Lightning strikes somewhere in the distance, revealing the entire ocean for one breathtaking instant.

The camera rises higher and higher while maintaining visual continuity.

The lighthouse becomes smaller beneath the gigantic storm clouds.

One final beam sweeps directly toward the camera, briefly filling the entire frame with golden-white light.

End naturally with the light passing across the lens while the storm continues behind .

 — like a lost scene from a $200-million Hollywood survival thriller.

title: Anime Action Sequence: Tiny Bar, Huge Problem (30-Second "Maximum Overreaction"…
prompt:
Anime Action Sequence: Tiny Bar, Huge Problem (30-Second "Maximum Overreaction" Version)

[Key Highlights]: A brown anime T-rex in a white fedora and Hawaiian shirt performs at a tiny Puerto Rico waterside bar, gradually turning a cheerful acoustic set into an absurdly overpowered anime battle spectacle. A drunk tourist attempts to join the performance and accidentally becomes part of the escalating chaos before the T-rex unleashes an outrageously unnecessary guitar-based finishing move.

[Style]: anime action-comedy spectacle; hyper-dramatic framing; crisp cel animation; elite shonen battle visuals; exaggerated expressions; rapid-fire editing; strong comedic timing; tropical daylight setting; spectacular music-driven VFX; non-gory/bloodless.

[Duration]: 30 seconds

[Setting]: A cheerful small waterside bar in Puerto Rico with blue sky, sparkling turquoise sea, palm trees, bright colorful decor, tourists and locals packed around a miniature wooden stage.

[00:00-00:05] Shot 1: "Unassuming Menace" — Introduction

Visuals: Handheld camera, medium angle. A brown anime T-rex wearing a white fedora and Hawaiian shirt strums an acoustic guitar on the tiny stage. It is weird but delightful. The crowd claps, laughs, raises drinks, and sways casually to the music.

Action: The dinosaur hits a warm, friendly opening chord. Then a second chord detonates a circular blast of wind so strong that napkins, maracas, cocktail umbrellas, and someone’s straw hat rocket into the air.

The T-rex does not react at all. It simply keeps strumming perfectly in rhythm.

VFX Details: Anime shockwave ring, fluttering props, sudden impact frame, subtle golden aura blooming behind the dinosaur, dramatic speed lines radiating outward.

[00:05-00:10] Shot 2: "One More Mojito" — The Challenger Appears

Visuals: A sunburned, middle-aged tourist in a loud floral shirt staggers enthusiastically out of the crowd holding a half-finished tropical drink. He is clearly having the greatest vacation of his life.

Action: Inspired by the music, he attempts an ambitious salsa dance directly in front of the stage.

For approximately two seconds, he is surprisingly good.

Then the T-rex hits another enormous chord.

The tourist attempts a dramatic spin, loses his balance completely, pinwheels his arms, accidentally spins twice more, and crashes harmlessly backward into a pile of inflatable pool floats.

His drink somehow remains perfectly upright.

He raises it triumphantly from inside the pile.

The crowd ROARS.

VFX Details: Comedic anime speed lines around the spinning tourist, exaggerated slow-motion wobble, sparkling drink trajectory, enormous reaction faces from nearby patrons, tiny celebratory impact flash when he lands.

[00:10-00:15] Shot 3: "String Theory Catastrophe" — Attack Sequence

Visuals: Rapid close-ups of vibrating guitar strings, dinosaur claws, narrowed T-rex eye, stomping feet, rattling bottles, and the increasingly horrified face of a decorative wooden parrot mounted beside the bar.

Action: The T-rex suddenly launches into a blistering guitar solo.

Each strum produces visible crescent-shaped musical slashes that rip through the humid tropical air.

The stage cracks beneath its feet.

Bar stools slide backward.

Palm trees bend.

The sea begins churning in the distance.

The drunk tourist, now back on his feet, tries to dance again and is immediately blown backward across the floor while still enthusiastically doing finger guns.

VFX Details: Glowing music-note trails, sharp anime impact flashes, fractured wood, tropical wind vortex, flower petals, bar receipts, napkins, and ice cubes spiraling upward.

[00:15-00:20] Shot 4: "Cretaceous Combo" — Total Escalation

Visuals: Camera rapidly orbits the stage as the T-rex swings the acoustic guitar like a legendary sword, Hawaiian shirt whipping dramatically behind it like a hero’s cape.

Action: The T-rex unleashes a sequence of increasingly ridiculous musical attacks:

– a downward strum sends a shockwave racing across the floor
– an upward chord launches tables several inches into the air
– a spinning guitar flourish creates a miniature tropical tornado
– one impossibly fast claw-picked riff makes every glass bottle behind the bar resonate in perfect harmony

The drunk tourist sees the tornado and tries to dance inside it.

He immediately spins uncontrollably through frame like a human top.

The bartender calmly ducks as he flies past.

VFX Details: Layered dinosaur afterimages, glowing guitar arcs, swirling palm leaves, airborne fruit slices, sparkling glass reflections, dramatic cel-animated energy trails.

[00:20-00:25] Shot 5: "The Ocean Answers" — Power-Up

Visuals: Suddenly, the camera drops into an extreme low-angle hero shot facing the ocean.

The T-rex plants one huge foot onto the cracked stage and raises the acoustic guitar overhead.

Its white fedora casts a shadow across its eyes.

For the first time, everything becomes completely still.

Action: The dinosaur slowly strums one impossibly deep chord.

The ocean behind the bar begins to rise.

A massive wall of turquoise water forms offshore.

Clouds spiral overhead.

Palm trees bow toward the stage.

Every loose object in the bar begins levitating.

The drunk tourist floats several inches off the ground, still holding his drink, looks down in confusion, then casually takes another sip.

The crowd realizes something enormous is coming.

VFX Details: Huge glowing aura, ocean energy spirals, vibrating air distortion, levitating debris, electric musical symbols orbiting the guitar, dramatic close-up of the T-rex opening one eye.

[00:25-00:30] Shot 6: "Finishing Move: Boricua Riff Ragnarok" — Final Impact

Visuals: Hero shot against the blazing tropical sky and towering wall of ocean water.

The T-rex swings the guitar downward and strikes one final catastrophic power chord.

Action: A gigantic spectral dinosaur made entirely of sound waves, turquoise seawater, sunlight, and glowing guitar strings erupts from the stage.

The apparition ROARS silently and surges across the bar before racing outward over the ocean in an enormous radiant wave.

The entire environment explodes into swirling sea spray, music notes, napkins, palm leaves, flower petals, and golden light.

Then:

Instant silence.

Everything gently falls back into place.

The ocean becomes perfectly calm.

The T-rex lowers the guitar.

It carefully adjusts its white fedora.

Behind it, the drunk tourist drops harmlessly out of the air into a beach chair.

His drink is still intact.

He takes one final sip.

A beat.

The entire bar ERUPTS into deafening applause and celebration.

Spectacular Effects: Colossal spectral energy dinosaur, gigantic ocean spray explosion, blue-gold musical lightning, extreme anime impact frame, radiant tropical backlight, debris suspended in slow motion, followed by comic-perfect total silence and triumphant final applause.

title: Create a 20-second photorealistic, family-friendly jungle adventure in 16:9…
prompt:
Create a 20-second photorealistic, family-friendly jungle adventure in 16:9 widescreen.
FORMAT AND POV:
Text-to-video. One continuous, uninterrupted first-person POV recording with no cuts, transitions, montage, slow motion or changes of viewpoint.
The camera is a handheld DSLR operated by an unseen safari guest sitting in the centre of the back seat of an open-top jeep. The lens looks forward between the two front seats. The camera continues recording throughout the entire adventure.
GROUND-LEVEL ENVIRONMENT:
The first frame begins inside a dense tropical jungle at ground level. All four tyres of the jeep are travelling along a wet, muddy trail surrounded by thick vegetation. Puddles, exposed roots, ferns and hanging vines are visible ahead.
The vehicle remains on the jungle floor. The environment feels humid and immense, with soft morning sunlight filtering naturally through the canopy.
CHARACTERS:
Exactly two adult women sit in the front of the jeep.
The curly brown-haired woman drives from the front-left seat. She wears a dusty grey tank top and practical adventure clothing.
The straight black-haired woman sits in the front-right passenger seat. She wears a dark olive expedition shirt and practical safari gear.
Keep their faces, hair, clothing, proportions and seat positions consistent. Both women remain safe and stay inside the jeep for the entire video.
CONTINUOUS ACTION:
The recording opens with the jeep already moving along the muddy jungle trail. Its tyres splash through shallow puddles while vines gently brush the sides of the vehicle.
Colossal elephants slowly emerge from the misty vegetation ahead. They are recognisable modern elephants with realistic anatomy, natural skin and believable movement, but several times larger than normal. Their enormous legs resemble moving pillars among the jungle trees.
The jeep carefully drives between the elephants. One elephant places its enormous foot into a puddle beside the vehicle, producing a spectacular splash of muddy water. Another elephant gently extends its trunk over the open jeep and sprays a fine shower of water across the passengers and camera lens. The surprised women duck, then laugh with amazement as the peaceful elephants continue through the jungle.
A deep gorilla call echoes behind the jeep.
The camera operator quickly turns around. One gigantic but curious silverback gorilla steps onto the jungle trail. It has realistic anatomy, natural wet black fur and powerful physical weight. It notices a canvas supply bag filled with colourful tropical fruit swinging from the rear of the jeep.
The curious gorilla begins bounding along the trail behind the moving vehicle, interested only in the fruit bag. It keeps a safe distance from the passengers while moving through the vegetation with impressive speed.
The camera whips forward again. The brunette driver looks back briefly, smiles nervously, accelerates and shouts:
“Hold on!”
The jeep moves faster through the jungle. Mud sprays from the tyres, hanging leaves sweep past the lens and the passenger grips the dashboard with excited laughter.
The camera turns backward once more. The gorilla reaches the loose canvas strap, gently pulls the fruit bag free and immediately slows down. It sits in the middle of the trail, happily examining the fruit as the jeep continues away. The encounter feels exciting and playful rather than hostile.
The jeep drives into a shallow jungle river and splashes toward a bright clearing. Sunlight blooms across the wet lens. Both women laugh with relief while the camera returns to the forward view between their seats.
Suddenly, leaves rustle on the riverbank above them. One enormous jaguar, approximately the size of a rhinoceros, makes a spectacular graceful leap from one side of the river to the other, passing directly over the open jeep.
The jaguar is a realistic modern animal with golden fur, black rosettes, natural feline anatomy and fluid movement. It does not land on the vehicle or touch the passengers.
As the jaguar passes overhead, its long tail sweeps extremely close to the lens. The startled operator’s wet hand loses its grip on the DSLR. The camera slips harmlessly over the side of the jeep and drops into the shallow river while continuing to record.
The POV enters the water with a large splash. Bubbles flow past the lens as the camera gently sinks and rolls. Through the rippling surface, show the jeep continuing safely across the shallow river while the giant jaguar stands calmly on the opposite bank, looking back.
End underwater with rising bubbles, refracted sunlight, muffled laughter and the enormous jaguar’s distorted silhouette above the surface.
CAMERA STYLE:
Authentic handheld DSLR safari footage with moderate natural shaking, quick human reaction pans and realistic movement created by the travelling jeep.
Use brief autofocus hunting, natural motion blur, water droplets on the lens, realistic exposure adjustment and convincing underwater refraction. Keep every important animal action understandable.
All camera movement must be physically motivated by the jeep or the camera operator. Maintain one continuous recording.
AUDIO:
Natural environmental audio only. Include the jeep engine, wet tyres, jungle birds, insects, rustling leaves, elephant footsteps, water splashes, the elephant’s soft rumble, the gorilla’s distant call, excited reactions, the driver saying “Hold on!”, laughter, rushing river water and muffled underwater bubbles.
No music, narration or additional dialogue.
VISUAL STYLE:
Extremely photorealistic live-action footage. Realistic human skin, individual hair strands, wet fabric, elephant skin, gorilla fur, jaguar fur, scratched vehicle metal, muddy tyres, tropical leaves, atmospheric mist and natural water behaviour.
The animals remain recognisable present-day animals, simply enlarged to an extraordinary scale. Their sizes remain consistent relative to the jeep.
The emotional progression is wonder, playful excitement, fast movement, relief and a final breathtaking surprise.
TECHNICAL LOCK:
One continuous POV take. Ground-level jungle travel throughout. Exactly two women, several peaceful giant elephants, one curious giant gorilla and one giant jaguar. Consistent characters, vehicle and animal anatomy. No elevated roadway, external camera angle, duplication, transformation, subtitles, logos, watermarks or on-screen text.

15.0-18.7s SHOT 5 — 8°, camera 0.4m from her eyes at 1.5m, static. Her eyes at x50 y50. The lower rims go glassy and hold, the surface trembling without falling. One slow blink pushes a single tear onto the lash line and it runs into the crease below. Her gaze does not move. HARD CUT.

18.7-22.5s SHOT 6 — 18°, camera 1.2m from her face at 1.5m, static. at x50 y48. Her whole face breaks upward — a short wet laugh at something he said, teeth showing, eyes crumpling shut, one shoulder lifting. Her wet cheeks catch the light as she laughs. HARD CUT.

0–5 秒：清晨从云南大理的民宿出发。主角背着小背包，从带木门、白墙、绿植和院落感的温馨民宿走出来。她低头查看手机路线，然后抬头对着朋友的镜头自然微笑，随手整理头发，向巷子外走去。镜头从后方和侧后方跟拍，有朋友手持拍摄的轻微晃动。画面里有清晨柔和阳光、安静石板路、白族风格建筑、街边绿植和刚开门的小店。环境声包括鸟叫、远处人声、脚步声和清晨街道声音。

5–11 秒：大理古城街道探索。镜头跟随她在古城街道慢慢走。两侧有白墙灰瓦、木质招牌、鲜花、小咖啡馆、云南小吃店和游客。她走进一家小咖啡馆或街边饮品店，买一杯饮料，接过饮料时自然地笑。她对着镜头简单说一句中文：“今天先去洱海。”然后继续走过街头小店，停下来拍一张照片，低头看相机预览，又忍不住笑。镜头保持近距离，捕捉不经意的真实瞬间，不要摆拍。

11–18 秒：前往洱海。环境从古城街道自然过渡到洱海边的公路和开阔湖景。主角坐在电动车后座或步行来到洱海边，海风吹动她的头发。她第一次看到洱海时明显变得兴奋，回头看向镜头笑，然后快步走向湖边。镜头跟随她走在洱海生态廊道上，旁边有蓝色湖面、远处苍山、白色栏杆、树影和骑行的人。她停下来望向湖面，拿手机拍照，手扶栏杆，表情自然放松。环境声有风声、湖水声、自行车经过声和远处游客说话声。

18–24 秒：喜洲稻田和白族村落午后。镜头切到阳光下的稻田小路，主角和朋友一起走在田边。背景有绿色稻田、白族民居、远山、蓝天和慢慢移动的云。她蹲下看路边小花，起身时回头对镜头笑。她和朋友在村口小摊买当地小吃，边走边吃，表情真实轻松。镜头在人群和小巷之间自然移动，偶尔轻微晃动，像朋友随手记录旅行片段。不要刻意设计动作，不要夸张表演。

24–30 秒：洱海日落结束时刻。金色傍晚，主角坐在洱海边或湖边长椅上，手里拿着饮料，安静看日落。湖面有细碎波光，远处是苍山轮廓和晚霞。朋友的镜头从她侧后方慢慢后退，先拍到她的侧脸和被风吹动的头发，再带出洱海、天空和宁静傍晚景色。最后她回头看向镜头，轻轻笑一下，说一句中文：“云南真的好舒服。”画面停留在真实旅行回忆感上，温暖、松弛、自然。

视觉风格：真实个人旅行 Vlog 素材，像智能手机或小型无反相机拍摄。自然日光，真实曝光，轻微手持晃动，随意构图，真实真人反应，纪录片式写实风格。不要电影商业质感，不要精致广告大片感，不要刻意摆拍姿势，不要人工转场特效，不要文字叠加，不要 Logo，不要水印。

全程保持参考图女性的面部身份、发型、五官、肤色、身材比例和自然表情一致。不要换脸，不要变成其他女性，不要过度美颜，不要二次元，不要网红滤镜感。全程无字幕、无背景音乐，仅保留真实环境声、脚步声、风声、人声、市集声、湖水声、鸟叫声和朋友拍摄时的自然声音。

The woman from Image 1 wears an oversized cotton T-shirt, navy cotton shorts, and rubber slides. Late at night, she waits alone in a small self-service laundromat for the last few minutes of a dryer cycle. An empty plastic laundry basket rests on her knees, and a cold drink can sits beside her. When the dryer buzzer sounds, she unloads the hot laundry, buries her face in its warmth, then notices one sock is missing while folding. She retrieves it from the back of the dryer drum before leaving. The mood progresses naturally from quiet boredom, to small comfort, to mild relief.
Shot 1 (0–2s):
She is already moving. One thumb scrolls through her phone while her bare heel bounces a rubber slide against the tiled floor. The empty laundry basket rests on her knees, and the dryer spins behind her. She quietly says in Korean: "아, 이거 언제 끝나…" ("Ah... when is this going to finish?"). A low handheld camera glides along the bench while the blurred rim of the basket crosses the foreground.
Shot 2 (2–4s):
She places the phone face down on the bench, opens a cold can one-handed, and takes a drink while glancing at the dryer's countdown timer. The camera slowly pushes from her hand to her face as autofocus catches up a beat late.
Shot 3 (4–6s):
The dryer sounds three flat buzzer tones. She swallows, sets the can down, stands up, tucks the basket under one arm, and walks to the dryer. The camera swings toward the machine, overshoots slightly, then naturally corrects back onto her.
Shot 4 (6–8s):
She pulls the dryer door open, and a rush of hot air hits her face. She instinctively jerks her hand back and shakes it. Looking at the laundry, she says in Korean: "앗, 뜨거." ("Ah, hot."). She immediately reaches back in. The camera observes over her shoulder and wobbles slightly as she pulls the clothes free.
Shot 5 (8–11s):
She lifts an armful of hot laundry into the basket, buries her face in the warm pile, and inhales deeply. Smiling to herself, she says: "아, 좋다…" ("Ah... that's nice."). She lifts her head and laughs softly at herself. The camera moves close from the side, with loose strands of hair and faint steam softly blurring the foreground.
Shot 6 (11–13s):
Back on the bench, she folds quickly, matching socks by touch. She suddenly holds up one unmatched sock, then scans the floor and underneath the bench. She says in Korean: "어, 양말 하나 어디 갔어." ("Huh? Where did one sock go?"). The camera starts on her hands and tilts up to her face as she looks around.
Shot 7 (13–15s):
She returns to the dryer, reaches deep into the back of the drum, and pulls out the missing sock. She waves it once, lets out a short amused snort, hooks the basket onto her hip, and exits through the glass door into the dark street. The camera drops low beneath her elbow and tilts upward as it follows her outside.

Only raw production sound: the low rumble of the dryer, another machine humming, fluorescent light hiss, thumb taps on the phone, a drink can opening, three flat buzzer tones, the metal dryer door opening, hot fabric rustling, the woman's four Korean lines delivered clearly with accurate lip sync, a brief genuine laugh, rubber slides scuffing the tile floor, and one passing car outside. title: 28 seconds. 16:9. Amateur behind-the-scenes phone video shot inside an enormous…
prompt:
28 seconds. 16:9. Amateur behind-the-scenes phone video shot inside an enormous film soundstage. Handheld, kinetic, one continuous take, phone-camera image quality — not cinematic.

THE MODEL: A colossal practical miniature of Lower Manhattan built into a long concrete water tank set flush into the stage floor. This is a large-scale build, not a tabletop — the financial district towers stand between four and nine metres tall, and the crew walking the catwalks alongside them are dwarfed, reaching only partway up the lower buildings. Geography is accurate: the island tapers to a point at Battery Park at the left-hand end and widens to the right, the dense financial district cluster rising just behind the tip, avenues running true in a clear grid, and the Brooklyn and Manhattan bridges springing east across the tank water behind the island to a low Brooklyn shore.

The build is convincingly weathered — streaked concrete, water-stained stone, rust on fire escapes, grime around window frames. Rooftops carry full clutter: HVAC units, water towers, vents, aerials, cables. Model traffic sits in the streets. Nothing is new or clean.

CAMERA POSITION: at the tank rail on the model's west side, held by a crew member, not rigged. The island runs broadside across the frame — seen in profile, left to right, not receding into depth. Crew on the near catwalk pass through the foreground in silhouette.

THE GATE: at the far left corner of the tank, diagonally opposite the camera, a colossal steel sluice gate is set into the tank wall — twelve metres wide, scarred and rust-streaked, holding back a full reservoir. Hydraulic rams on either side. Amber warning beacons above.

THE STAGE: blue cyclorama with orange tracking crosses beyond the model. A technocrane overhead. Crew in plain grey shirts. Work lights on stands, cables taped down.

SEQUENCE — 28 SECONDS
0-6s     ESTABLISH SCALE. The stage is quiet, the model dry. The camera tracks slowly left to right along the length of the island in profile, the whole skyline reading across the frame. A crew member walks the near catwalk through the foreground and is plainly, obviously smaller than the towers behind them. The camera tilts up the tallest tower and the top is far above head height.
6-9s     THE GATE. The operator pans left to the far corner. The steel gate fills that end of the tank. Amber beacons start turning. A klaxon sounds twice. Crew step back. Someone off-camera calls "clear."
9-11s    ACTION. A voice off-camera calls "Action." The hydraulic rams haul the gate upward, steel screaming against steel.
11-14s   RELEASE. Water blasts out beneath the rising gate under enormous pressure — a solid white wall, not a build-up. It enters at the top left of frame and immediately runs diagonally across the tank, the front cutting toward the near-right and gaining height as it comes.
14-22s   IMPACT, IN PROFILE. The wave strikes the island along its western flank. Seen side-on, the front stands roughly two thirds the height of the tallest towers — the comparison is direct and unmistakable. Battery Park goes under first at frame-left, then the impact runs rightward along the island like a fuse. Towers shear at the base and topple toward camera with real weight and real slowness, four and nine metre structures going over one after another. Water surges up the avenues between them. Both bridge spans lift off their piers and break. Debris the size of furniture tumbles in the flow. The leading edge reaches the near tank wall and comes over the rail at the camera — the operator shouts, stumbles backward, and the frame swings wildly before recovering.
22-28s   AFTERMATH. The surge subsides. Broken tower sections circle slowly in the tank. Water pours off the cyclorama edge and drains across the stage floor. Someone laughs off-camera. Two crew walk into frame in waders. The operator keeps filming several seconds too long.

IMAGE: deep depth of field throughout — everything from the near rail to the far cyclorama stays sharp. No shallow focus, no macro, no tilt-shift. Faint atmospheric haze at the far end of the stage. Phone-camera characteristics: aggressive auto-exposure, highlight clipping on the work lights, digital noise in the shadows.

AUDIO: diegetic only — stage hum, the klaxon, the off-camera "clear" and "Action", steel grinding as the gate lifts, the enormous release of water, tower sections cracking and going over in sequence, water pouring over concrete, crew shouting and laughing, the phone mic distorting badly on the loudest moment. No music, no narration.

CONSTRAINTS: the island is seen broadside in profile, never head-on and never receding into depth. The tank is set into the stage floor — never on a table, trestles, benches or any raised surface. The model buildings are taller than the crew, always. No people in the model, no model figures, no casualties, no injury. No readable signage or brand marks on any building. No brand marks on crew clothing. One continuous take, no cuts. No slow motion, no tilt-shift.

七戒：她指上的七枚戒指同时脱落并在空中放大成七道巨型金环，以不同轴向旋转直至完全同心对齐，对齐瞬间自环心射出一道贯穿全场的光柱。

【VFX等级】体积火焰具备浮力与涡流，金线与金环为有厚度与自阴影的立体金属，浓烟为体积雾并受气流推动；所有特效都有生成、扩散、消散三个阶段，且持续累积绝不消失。

0-2秒｜极端微距接快速后拉、100mm至35mm：画面开场是她的眼睛占满全屏，瞳孔中倒映着整排歪斜的烛火；她眼睑抬起的瞬间，镜头后拉，她视线扫过的石柱表面被金色纹样瞬间蚀刻并向四周蔓延，地砖成片浮起，蜡滴倒着升空。
2-4秒｜低角度仰拍接缓慢环绕、35mm：【烛卫】发动——全场烛焰同时脱离烛芯，各自化作巴掌大的火焰战士剪影悬停半空，成千上万个同时转身面朝她；她自王座起身，扶手爆出裂纹，金色丝缕自铠甲不断升腾。
4-6秒｜贴身微距横移接急速拉远、100mm至24mm：【金织】发动——镜头贴着她的肩甲，金色浮雕纹路自边缘剥离抽成活的金线并擦过镜头射向空中；急速拉远，露出金线在整座大厅内编织成的巨型立体网格，她立于正中央。
6-8秒｜正面推轨接主观穿越、50mm：【七戒】发动——七枚戒指自她指间弹开并在空中放大成七道巨型金环，各自旋转对齐；镜头自最外环的环心一路穿过全部七环直抵她面前，对齐完成的瞬间光柱自她身前射出贯穿大厅，石柱成排爆碎。
8-10秒｜自她身后越肩仰拍、28mm：【骸息】发动——王座上的骷髅同时张口喷出黑烟，在她身后汇聚成数十米高的巨大骷髅并睁开燃烧的眼窝；同时穹顶开始裂开，白色天光自裂缝渗入，火焰战士群与金色网格在光中同时显形。
10-12秒｜自穹顶破口向下坠落的俯拍、24mm：穹顶被彻底击碎，巨大的白色天光柱灌满大厅，黑暗被瞬间驱散；镜头俯冲向下，她的铠甲逐片分离悬浮在体表之外，缝隙中涌出熔金般流动的炽白光，四种技能的特效同时悬停在她周围绝不消失。
12-14秒｜自巨骷髅眼窝内向外拍摄接绕至正面、35mm：黑色皮草披风解体化作黑烟与余烬构成的巨大羽翼在天光中展开；王冠向上生长成一圈旋转的金色符文光环，七道金环同时收拢环绕她的身体，双眼燃起炽白火焰；她抛光的铠甲映出整座被光贯穿的大厅。
14-15秒｜极低角度仰拍急速推近至定格、24mm：她向前踏出一步，火焰战士群、金色网格、七道金环与巨大骷髅同时随她的动作向前压出；冲击波把所有特效一次性推向四周并在空中静止；她抬眼直视镜头，画面定格在她的正面英雄构图上。

【约束】全片视觉重心始终在她身上，特效必须围绕她展开而非喧宾夺主；四式技能的特效一旦出现便持续存在并叠加，绝不消失或重置；第10秒之后画面保持明亮通透；人物五官、发型、铠甲与配饰全程与参考图完全一致；动作沉稳克制、有重量与惯性，杜绝任何僵硬或不自然的关节角度；画面无字幕、无文字、无水印。

title: 生成一支15秒、16:9横版的创意中文字体商业短片。整体为顶级真实摄影质感，快速但清晰的节奏，三个场景具有明显不同的材质、色彩与光线。全片由同一只干净纤细的女性…
prompt:
生成一支15秒、16:9横版的创意中文字体商业短片。整体为顶级真实摄影质感，快速但清晰的节奏，三个场景具有明显不同的材质、色彩与光线。全片由同一只干净纤细的女性右手，握着同一支透明玻璃笔完成书写，不露脸。手部外观、肤色、指甲、握笔姿势、玻璃笔结构和笔尖造型全程完全一致。

核心文字：“点个赞”。

笔尖接触不同材质时，墨水会转化成对应环境中的自然元素。三个汉字必须按照标准简体中文结构和正常书写顺序，由笔尖真实接触表面逐笔完成。

【音乐】

生成原创15秒背景音乐，轻盈、现代、梦幻、有高级科技品牌短片质感。使用清脆木琴、玻璃敲击、冷感电子脉冲、细腻弦乐拨奏和温暖合成器。

音乐划分为三个明确章节：

0–4秒：星空场景使用轻盈木琴与玻璃音色。

4秒转场时加入一次清脆低频鼓点，进入雨夜城市后叠加冷蓝色电子脉冲。

8秒转场时音乐快速上扬，进入云海日出后加入明亮弦乐和温暖合成器。

“赞”字最后一笔完成时，音乐达到最高点，并以一次短促、明亮、有力量的电影和弦收尾。所有笔尖落下、文字完成和画面转场都必须踩准音乐重拍。无人声、无歌词、不模仿任何现有旋律。

【音效】

保留玻璃笔与不同表面接触的清晰摩擦声、星尘流动声、雨水敲击车窗声、城市远处环境声、云层穿越声和最终阳光爆发的低频冲击声。音效与音乐同时存在，但落笔声和转场声音必须清楚可辨。

【镜头1：点】

0–4秒。极致微距摄影。

同一只女性右手握着透明玻璃笔，在悬浮于深空中的黑色透明玻璃板上，完整、端正地写出简体中文“点”。

笔尖划过的位置不是普通墨水，而是由金色星尘、微小星云和发光粒子组成的笔画。笔尖移动时，远处沉睡的星星依次亮起；已经写出的笔画稳定保留，不能消失或漂移。

“点”字最后一点落下时，整片星空同时闪亮。一颗耀眼星光从最后一点快速冲向镜头，纯白光线完全覆盖画面并保持0.2秒。

【镜头2：个】

4–8秒。用上一镜的白色星光进行全白遮挡转场。

白光退去后，场景瞬间变成雨夜都市。同一支玻璃笔保持上一镜相同的运动方向，在布满雨珠的电车车窗上，完整写出端正清晰的简体中文“个”。

笔画呈冷蓝色霓虹材质，真实照亮手指、玻璃雨珠和窗外城市。笔尖每完成一笔，窗外一排建筑灯光便同步亮起。已经写出的蓝色笔画必须稳定、清晰，雨水不能冲散文字。

“个”字最后一笔完成时，霓虹笔画释放一圈蓝色光波。光波沿车窗快速扩散，最终形成一整面纯蓝色光幕并完全遮满镜头。

【镜头3：赞】

8–13秒。用蓝色光幕进行颜色与运动方向一致的匹配转场。

蓝光退去后，场景变成清晨云海之上的巨大透明冰面。同一只右手、同一支玻璃笔，在覆盖白霜的透明冰面上，按照正确笔画顺序完整写出简体中文“赞”。

镜头保持近距离俯拍，确保整个“赞”字始终位于画面中央并完整可见。笔尖划过时擦掉冰霜，露出冰层下方流动的温暖金光。每一笔都必须连接正确、结构端正；已经完成的复杂笔画不能合并、减少、重排或变形。

“赞”字最后一笔完成时，远处太阳从云海后迅速升起。金色阳光穿透整个“赞”字，冰面内部产生真实折射，温暖光线直射镜头。

【结尾】

13–15秒。摄影机从金色光线中快速拉远。

星空、雨夜城市、云海日出三个场景组成三个并列的竖向电影画格。左侧画格完整保留金色星尘组成的“点”，中间画格完整保留蓝色霓虹组成的“个”，右侧画格完整保留冰面金光组成的“赞”。

三个字从左到右组合成唯一一句完整、清晰、顺序正确的中文：

“点个赞”

三个画格中的环境仍有轻微自然运动，但文字完全静止。画面稳定停留至少1.5秒后，在音乐明亮和弦中结束。

【文字铁律】

全片只能出现“点”“个”“赞”三个简体中文汉字，不得出现任何其他文字、字母、数字、标点、Logo、字幕或符号。

每个字必须由笔尖真实接触表面并逐笔写出，字形端正、结构正确、笔画数量准确、清晰可读。文字不能凭空出现。笔尖未经过的位置不能提前产生笔画。

已经写出的笔画不得消失、漂移、闪烁、增生、重排、变形或被快速转场永久遮挡。最终三个字必须按照“点个赞”的顺序完整保留。

禁止左手写字、手部切换、玻璃笔变形、握笔方式变化、多余手指、错误汉字、繁体字、书法草写、英文、贴纸、点赞图标、爱心符号、人物露脸、卡通风格、廉价粒子、普通蒙版转场和水印。

prompt:
Create a 30-second cinematic animated short film using the provided character as the exact visual reference. Preserve the character’s appearance throughout the entire video: a cheerful, slightly clumsy cartoon chef with a large curled black mustache, white chef hat, white chef uniform, black neckerchief, white apron, black-and-white checkered pants, black shoes, and an enormous wooden rolling pin almost as large as his body.

The world is a whimsical minimalist kitchen-inspired fantasy environment with a warm golden-yellow background, soft cream clouds, subtle paper texture, vintage storybook aesthetics, and playful surreal details. The animation should feel like a high-end children’s animated short with expressive body language, polished 3D character animation, cinematic lighting, tactile materials, and gentle humor.

Important: Keep the character’s face, clothing, mustache, chef hat, body proportions, and rolling pin design consistent. No character redesign, no extra characters, no text, no subtitles, no logos.

0–4 SEC — THE BIG IDEA

Shot: Wide cinematic establishing shot.

The chef stands alone in his tiny whimsical kitchen, staring proudly at a small lump of dough sitting on a wooden table.

He slowly looks from the tiny dough to his enormous rolling pin.

His eyes widen.

He gets a mischievous smile.

Camera: slow push-in toward his face.

Animation: subtle eyebrow movement, mustache bouncing slightly as he smiles, exaggerated cartoon expression.

Sound: soft magical chime followed by a playful comedic beat.

4–9 SEC — THE FIRST ROLL

The chef dramatically grabs the enormous rolling pin with both hands.

He struggles to lift it.

His body leans backward from the weight.

Then—

WHOOSH!

He swings the rolling pin forward and begins rolling the tiny piece of dough.

The rolling pin moves across the table with ridiculous force.

The dough rapidly expands.

Camera: low-angle tracking shot following the rolling pin.

The chef’s eyes become wider and wider as he realizes the dough is getting way too big.

9–14 SEC — IT GETS OUT OF CONTROL

The dough suddenly becomes enormous.

It spreads across the entire table.

Then over the edge.

Then across the kitchen floor.

The chef tries desperately to stop the rolling pin.

But the giant rolling pin keeps spinning.

He gets dragged forward.

His little black shoes slide across the floor.

His chef hat tilts sideways.

His mustache shakes dramatically.

Camera: dynamic side-tracking shot with slight comedic handheld movement.

The chef finally loses his grip.

The giant rolling pin rolls away by itself.

14–19 SEC — THE GIANT DOUGH

The chef runs after the rolling pin.

He suddenly stops.

His expression changes from panic to complete amazement.

Reveal a massive perfectly rolled sheet of dough stretching across the golden landscape like a giant blanket.

The chef slowly walks toward it.

He touches it with one finger.

BOING.

The dough gently bounces.

His eyes sparkle.

He realizes he accidentally created something incredible.

Camera: slow cinematic crane upward revealing the enormous scale of the dough.

19–25 SEC — THE CRAZY SOLUTION

The chef suddenly gets an idea.

He grabs the giant rolling pin again.

With exaggerated determination, he begins shaping the enormous dough.

Quick cinematic montage:

He rolls it forward.
He spins around it.
He jumps over the rolling pin.
He presses the dough into shape.
Flour bursts into the air like magical dust.
The chef emerges from the flour cloud looking extremely proud.

Camera: energetic quick cuts mixed with one smooth circular camera move.

Keep the action readable and comedic, not chaotic.

25–30 SEC — THE REVEAL

Final reveal:

The gigantic dough has transformed into an enormous perfect golden croissant-shaped pastry sitting in the middle of the whimsical yellow landscape.

The chef stands beside it, tiny in comparison.

He puts one hand on his hip and proudly holds the giant rolling pin over his shoulder.

He gives the camera a confident smile.

Suddenly—

PFFFT!

A tiny puff of flour lands directly on his mustache.

He freezes.

Looks cross-eyed at the flour.

Then casually wipes it away and poses proudly again.

Camera: slow cinematic pull-back revealing the chef, gigantic pastry, floating cream clouds, and tiny hot-air balloon in the background.

Ending: warm golden light, gentle magical particles, playful orchestral music resolving with a comedic final note.

Five seconds later, a colossal shockwave races toward the city and destroys everything. The destruction should feel overwhelming, sudden, and apocalyptic. At the exact peak of impact, the image freezes. Then the screen cuts to black.

Hyper-realistic, as if recorded on a real smartphone in one continuous handheld take. prompt:
[Global Setting] Base Environment & Texture: A professional boxing ring under 
hot arena lighting, dark spectator shadows in background, rope texture catching 
light, canvas floor worn and chalked, thick humid air visible in light shafts, 
amber/gold overhead rigs dominating, ring posts in each corner, referee visible 
at edge ready to watch.

[Opening beat, 0–5s]: Wide shot from corner camera angle, static. Two boxers 
in fighting stance face-to-face in the ring center, shoulders squared, muscles 
tense, breath visible in the humid air, crowd murmur building in background. 
Camera holds neutral, both fighters locked and waiting.

[Mid beat A ,Normal speed (5–12s)]: Boxer 1 throws a sharp jab, camera whips 
to follow, handheld energy. Boxer 2 slips and counters with a heavy body shot 
that forces air out. Quick exchanges of hooks and body shots, handheld camera 
movement tight and urgent following the intensity. Both fighters breathing hard. 
Sweat sprays with impacts, light catches wet skin and muscle.

[Mid beat B ,SLOW MOTION SECTION (12–18s)]: Boxer 1 throws a devastating 
overhead right hand aimed at Boxer 2's jaw. Time slows to 40% normal speed. 
Camera orbits slowly around the punch trajectory, capturing the full extension 
of the arm, the facial expression of concentration on Boxer 1's face, Boxer 2's 
eyes widening as they see it coming. The glove connects with the cheek in 
crystalline detail ,impact ripples across the jaw, sweat sprays in slow arcs, 
head snaps back violently, entire body recoils from the force. The moment stretches. 
Return to normal speed.

[Mid beat C , Normal speed (18–26s)]: Boxer 2 staggers back into the ropes, 
shaking their head to clear it, breathing heavily. Boxer 1 presses the 
advantage with a combination  left hook, right cross, series of body shots. 
Boxer 2 covers up, trying to recover. Ref moves closer to watch but doesn't 
step in yet. Brutal exchanges continue, both fighters exhausted and battered.

[Closing beat, 26–30s]: Both boxers breathing hard, moving slower now, arms 
heavy. Boxer 2 drops their guard slightly, Boxer 1 sees it but is equally 
destroyed. They circle once more, mutual respect and exhaustion in their eyes. 
Camera pulls to wide shot of the ring, both figures standing but barely, sweat 
dripping, the crowd roaring muffled. End on their locked stare.

Audio: Gloved punch impacts (clean sharp strikes mixed with heavy thuds), heavy 
labored breathing and exhales from both fighters, foot shuffle on canvas, crowd 
roar building and peaking, trainer shouts muffled at corners, bell distant ready 
to ring, during slow motion section: all sounds stretch and deepen (impact thud
